localChanges: chore: work towards a 3D map, not offered yet: under ?3d=1 Civ2's Explorers and Spies stand, walk and fall as the Partisans do, and the Explorer no longer carries a coil of rope (#1377)

log: This is the same tools/blender/rig.py as models-realistic-cc0's (civ-clone/models-realistic-cc0#33). Where a hold eases, the rig's report gives `slide`: the most, its largest step, the capped frames and the changes of sides. A slide that jumps sides by more than GRIP fails the build. Nothing here is rigged by rig.py, so no model changes.

The same tools/blender/split.py, tools/build.py and tools/check.py as models-realistic-cc0's, where the Explorer's coil of rope is dropped this way. A `split` may have only `drop` chains: nothing is then split off, no piece is written, and the body is staged by its own box. split.py fails if what such a rule drops moves that box by more than a millimetre, or if a rule would take every face. check.py ties a prop from the split, and "split off" in `made`, to chains, and a rule that only drops needs `made` to say what was dropped.
No model here uses it, so nothing changes.
Where a hold eases, the rig's report gives `slide` for each clip (fixes #31):
the most the holding hand slid along its prop (or moved it);
its largest change from one frame to the next;
how many frames it was capped, where the elbow falls short of the eased bend;
how many times it changed sides.

A slide that jumps from one side of where the shoulder comes nearest the prop's line to the other, by more than GRIP, fails the build. The rigged models rebuild unchanged. One fresh review; its findings are fixed.
The Explorer and the Spy now have idle, move and die clips, the Partisan's that I picked as the template for people. Neither fights.

The Explorer's coil of rope is gone from his belt. The cut to 2,000 triangles drew it as jagged slivers in his jacket's colour. It's dropped before the cut by a `split` rule that only drops, in four chains: down the middle of its loops, down each side, and at the top under the tie. His model has the open edges and loose triangles it had before, and no slivers at the hem. His jacket's owner colour now goes texel by texel, as the Rifleman's does, so it ends in a straight line at the hem rather than a zigzag. His static model changes, so the 3D map should repin.

split.py and check.py now allow a rule that only drops, and build.py stages the body by its own box then. split.py fails if what such a rule drops moves that box by more than a millimetre, or if a rule would take every face.
The other models rebuild unchanged. Two fresh reviews; their Medium is fixed, and the Lows are #35, #36 and #37.
